protocol: D-000 turn 1 of 3; refute not confirm; severable entries
summary: Both entries are severable and both draw objections. D-017's core act is not a restatement: its count-pinned three-member consumption rule exists in no cited source and silently omits D-001 Route A, so the RULE-GOVERNED label does not hold as written. D-018 bundles three severable preference-laden acts into one revert unit — the exact defect D-016 was created to prevent, and which this draft invokes against the four dispositions but not against itself — contains a step that contradicts D-001 SF-3's new-row rule, and imposes an undefined 'cannot gate' prohibition that exceeds D-002's own bytes. Every digest the draft quotes was re-measured and is correct; the INCOHERENT/7-blockers claim reproduces from the verdict bytes; 'integration half' is genuinely file 08's phrase, not a new split. The citation layer is clean. The decision-type and bundling layers are not.

objections.claim: D-017 is labelled RULE-GOVERNED on the ground that it 'restates rules already present', but its operative act — the count-pinned three-member consumption rule in Decision 3 — appears in none of the four sources it cites, and it silently drops D-001 Route A from the set of lawful vehicles.
objections.evidence: Draft L38-42 claims the entry 'restates rules already present in file 08's "only active checklist" paragraph, file 07's and file 10's competing-list disclaimers, file 11's own header, and D-001's definition of done.' Draft L60-69 then enumerates exactly three admissible vehicles: (1) a D-000 coordinator or product entry, (2) a register row or register amendment in file 08, (3) a reviewed pre-blueprint (Route B) disposition. Measured against COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md (3f449778932876ab5039c7f4b35a136a06a67c06b4e2ec00a70e95ae5f3c313f) L151-155, D-001's own enumeration is a DIFFERENT three: '(A) V1 successor through the coop process (author -> independent review -> coordinator apply -> freeze/claim-register motion); (B) an explicit, scoped, reviewed pre-blueprint disposition; (C) a product decision through the product-disposition process.' Route A is absent from the draft's list, and the draft's member 2 ('register row or register amendment') is not any of D-001's A/B/C. The omission is load-bearing, not cosmetic: file 11 items that are squarely Route A work — the section 3.1 supplier-coverage instrument, which binds freeze section 3.1 items to supplying V1 artifacts, and the hostile-input threat decision, which touches TM (freeze section 3 TM, still UNSET) — have no lawful path to becoming live work under a closed enumeration that excludes V1 successors. Creating a new closed routing constraint is a governance preference, not a restatement of an existing rule.
objections.proposedFix: Either (a) relabel D-017 PREFERENCE-LADEN for Decision 3 and carry it as its own isolated entry, or (b) restate Decision 3 to reference D-001's existing A/B/C routes plus, if a coordinator gate is genuinely intended, state that addition explicitly as a new rule with its own preference marking. If the closed enumeration is retained, add Route A as a member or state on the record which file 11 items are thereby made unroutable and why that is intended.

objections.claim: The 'count-pinned at three members' pin is not honest arithmetic: the three members are not disjoint, because member 2 collapses into member 1 under D-001 MF-6.
objections.evidence: Draft L60-69 pins the enumeration at three independent members. COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md L256-258 records MF-6: 'Register-content changes are DECISIONS, not hygiene (MF-6): the V1->V2 transition-contract row (V2TOPIC-F-02) and the DR-117 widening to file 02's seven binding items (V2TOPIC-F-04) each get their own D-000-reviewed entry and commit.' A register row or register amendment therefore cannot be created except through member 1. Member 3 (a reviewed Route B disposition) likewise requires a reviewed act. The draft itself relies on MF-6 at L74-76 to refuse wholesale gap import, so it accepts the premise that collapses its own member 2. The pin therefore counts three surface labels over what is operationally one gated vehicle, and 'any change to this enumeration re-opens this row' attaches to an enumeration whose members are not independent.
objections.proposedFix: Either restate the rule as one member ('a reviewed D-000-governed act, in one of the following forms') and drop the three-count pin, or keep three members and add an explicit sentence recording that member 2 is reachable only through member 1 per MF-6, so the pin is not read as three independent routes.

objections.claim: 'Any change to this enumeration re-opens this row' is a category slip: D-017 is a COORDINATOR-DECISIONS entry, and 'rows' are file 08 objects.
objections.evidence: Draft L60-61 (D-017 Decision 3) and L153-154 and L171-172 (D-018 Decision 4 and 6) each use 'this row'. File 08 (a3e37102991b80502aa1f9fb1affe2011859917b8ce1477a93f494485b9161b7) is where DR rows live; COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md carries entries, not rows. The count-pin idiom is borrowed from register practice (compare file 08 DR-117, 'count pinned at seven by COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md D-011', and DR-130's 'count-pinned 6/5/5') where 'row' is correct. Here it names nothing that exists.
objections.proposedFix: Replace 'this row' with 'this entry' in all three places, or state which file 08 row the pin is intended to re-open.

objections.claim: D-017 Decision 7 forward-references an entry dispatched in the same severable draft, so consenting D-017 while objecting to D-018 leaves the reference dangling.
objections.evidence: Draft L83-86: 'This entry creates no execution checklist. The next isolated preference-laden entry, if adopted, may name an execution sequence. That sequence, if adopted, lives in that entry.' The prompt and the draft header (L8-9) both establish that the entries are severable and may be consented independently. D-018 is that 'next entry' and is under the same review. The 'if adopted' hedging is present and correct, so this is not a false statement; it is a coupling that partially defeats the stated severability, since D-017's disclaimer is only meaningful once some later entry actually carries the sequence.
objections.proposedFix: No change required if the hedging is deemed sufficient. If tightened, drop the forward reference entirely — D-017 does not need it to state that it creates no checklist.

objections.claim: D-018 bundles three severable preference-laden acts into a single entry and a single revert unit, which is precisely the defect D-016 exists to prevent — and the draft invokes D-016 against bundling the four dispositions while committing the same error one level up.
objections.evidence: D-018 adopts three independently contestable preference-laden choices: (a) the naming of D-002's slice as 'architecture preview' (L129-136); (b) the selection of Route B for exactly four inherited rows (L149-164); (c) a count-pinned seven-step completion sequence (L171-204). The overturn clause at L248-249 offers 'one-line supersession here plus git revert of C-D018' — a revert that necessarily takes all three. COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md L1249-1255 records D-016's exact reasoning: 'The turn-1 draft carried it as part 4 of D-014 and declined the marking; both were wrong, and the turn-2 review showed why the bundling was not merely untidy: a decision recorded inside another decision's freeze rider cannot be overturned by reverting its own commit, so the overturn procedure would have been formal only.' The same sentence applies verbatim to (a), (b) and (c) here. The draft demonstrates it knows the rule: its Alternatives section at L225-227 rejects writing the four Route B dispositions inside this entry, reasoning 'Rejected: bundling; D-016's lesson; each disposition needs its own reviewed bytes.' The rule is applied downward and not to itself. A product owner who accepts the preview naming but rejects the Route B selection, or accepts both but rejects the seven-step order, has no revert path.
objections.proposedFix: Split into three entries: the preview naming; the Route B selection for the four named rows; the execution sequence. Each gets its own D-000 review and its own commit, per D-016 and D-001 SF-4. If the coordinator judges the naming and the Route B selection to be genuinely inseparable, that inseparability must be argued in bytes rather than assumed, and the sequence must in any case be severed.

objections.claim: Sequence step 6 contradicts D-001's SF-3 new-row rule, and therefore amends D-001 while the entry states it does not.
objections.evidence: Draft L199-201 (step 6): 'Recalculate file 08's condition-2 and condition-4 sets ONLY after a later successor that actually changes D-002's slice scope.' Measured against COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md L259-262, D-001 SF-3 reads: 'New-row rule (SF-3): condition 2's quantifier is evaluated over the register as it stands at readiness evaluation; adding a row is itself a reviewed decision under this protocol, so the quantifier can only grow by a recorded act, never by drift.' Under SF-3 the condition-2 set changes whenever a row is ADDED by a recorded act, with no D-002 scope change required — and this has already happened in practice: file 08 L368-373 records that D-010 amended condition 2's literal text and 'DR-130 joins the table', by the new-row rule and not by any D-002 scope change. Step 6's 'only after' therefore forbids a recalculation that D-001 mandates. D-017 Decision 4 (L70-72) asserts 'D-001 is not amended... This entry does not add, drop, or paraphrase those conditions', and D-018's own decision-type paragraph (L118-123) claims it does not change the condition-2 or condition-4 sets; the constraint on when those sets may be recomputed is an amendment in effect even though the current membership is untouched.
objections.proposedFix: Strike 'only' from step 6, or restate it as: 'This entry does not recalculate the condition-2 and condition-4 sets. They continue to be evaluated per D-001 SF-3 over the register as it stands at readiness evaluation, including any rows added by later recorded acts.'

objections.claim: Decision 3's prohibition on ever describing the slice as able to 'gate' exceeds D-002's adopted bytes, which surrender only baseline/ratchet gating, and it binds all future prose through an undefined term.
objections.evidence: Draft L143-146: 'No later document may describe the D-002 slice as the product that can gate, as OpenSIP MVP, or as upgrade continuity for opensip-cli users.' Measured against D-002's bytes in COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md (the T2-02 trade paragraph, file offsets 426-429): 'deferring it gives up the prototype's proven highest-leverage CI behavior — gating net-new findings against a recorded corpus — so slice 1 ships analysis WITHOUT RATCHETING, a materially weaker CI story.' D-002 gives up ratchet gating and describes what remains as materially weaker, not absent. The slice retains the surfaces that constitute gating: DR-123 is in its condition-2 set and mandates stable machine output and non-interactive CI behaviour with D9 exits; DR-G17 is in its condition-4 set and, per file 08's G17 row, requires the advertised SARIF projection to carry 'Run/Finding IDs, Coverage, verdict, truncation, artifact references' — so a verdict exists on the analyze surface. A blanket 'cannot gate' therefore removes product content D-002 retained, while Decision 2 (L137-142) claims the entry 'does not add or remove commands, language roles, platforms, deferrals, identity rides, or gates from D-002'. The term 'gate' is nowhere defined in the draft; on its plain reading it contradicts the adopted slice, and on a narrower intended reading (authoritative, sealed, ratcheted gating) it is simply unstated.
objections.proposedFix: Define the term and narrow the prohibition, e.g.: 'No later document may describe the D-002 slice as producing an authoritative sealed gate, as OpenSIP MVP, or as upgrade continuity for opensip-cli users. The slice does produce a verdict and D9 exit; what it cannot produce is a durable authoritative record of having gated, and it has no baseline/ratchet.' Confirm the wording against D-002's T2-02 paragraph rather than against file 11.

objections.claim: Decision 5 attributes authorizing power to Route B and attaches it to the wrong readiness condition.
objections.evidence: Draft L167-169: 'Route B authorizes at most a preview blueprint under D-001 condition 5.' Route B is condition 1's internal alternative, not an authorization instrument: file 08's readiness paragraph condition 1 reads 'DR-001 through DR-011 are SATISFIED or the owning V1 authority records an explicit, scoped, reviewed pre-blueprint disposition...', and condition 5 is the separate requirement that 'Product and architecture authorities explicitly authorize creation of docs/v2/implementation/ against a refreshed exact authority baseline.' Discharging condition 1 for four rows authorizes nothing on its own; conditions 2, 3, 4 and 5 remain independently required. The draft states the correct position elsewhere — Decision 3 (L147-148) says 'Condition 5 still forbids creating docs/v2/implementation/ until D-001's five conditions hold' — so this is an internal inconsistency rather than a settled position. The 'at most' limiter reduces the harm but does not repair the attribution.
objections.proposedFix: Restate as: 'Route B, once the dispositions are written and reviewed, can discharge condition 1 for the four named rows and nothing more. It does not authorize a blueprint of any kind; conditions 2 through 5 remain independently required, and condition 5 remains the only authorization for docs/v2/implementation/.'

objections.claim: Decision 7's consumption accounting of file 11's recommended sequence is inaccurate: item 1 is claimed as consumed while half of it is expressly not decided, and that half then appears in neither the consumed nor the remaining list.
objections.evidence: File 11 at ddcd1d3532fd1129c99356c5fd7f1acfab5f2787417392d40b4aa44251fd2cf5 carries eight recommended-sequence items at lines 301, 307, 312, 316, 322, 327, 333, 336. Item 1 (L301) is 'Decide preview versus MVP, AND decide the parallel-product posture.' Draft L206-212 claims steps 1-7 'consume file 11's recommended-sequence items 1, 2 (authorization to draft only), 4 (authorization to draft only), and the preview-versus-MVP naming', then lists as remaining '(narrow product successor, analyze contract, spike, section 3.1 supplier-coverage instrument, execution view)' = items 3, 5, 6, 7, 8. But the draft's own step 1 (L176-179) records 'Remaining isolated product entries, not decided here: parallel-product posture for opensip-cli; DR-117 successor / default-install shape.' Item 1 is therefore half-consumed, listed as consumed, and its undecided half is absent from the remaining list. The trailing clause 'and the preview-versus-MVP naming' is also redundant with item 1 itself, which obscures the split rather than disclosing it.
objections.proposedFix: Restate as: 'consumes file 11 item 1 in part (the preview-versus-MVP naming only; the parallel-product posture remains undecided and is carried at step 1), item 2 and item 4 as authorization to draft only. Remaining: the parallel-product posture half of item 1, and items 3, 5, 6, 7, 8.'

objections.claim: An alternative is rejected on the authority of a three-reviewer consensus that file 11's own bytes decline to assert.
objections.evidence: Draft L216-219 rejects 'Treat D-002 as product MVP and finish file 08 unchanged' with the reason 'Rejected: three independent reviews called that a product inversion'. File 11 does contain that merged sentence at L88-89 ('All three reviewers treat that as honest and as a product inversion'), but file 11's own Shared verdict at L25-28 qualifies it: 'All three reviewers converge on the core architectural destination and on the main sequencing risk. The remaining proposals vary in support and confidence; the attribution and disposition labels below preserve that difference rather than converting non-objection into consensus.' File 11's header (L3-5) further records 'Status: NON-BINDING SYNTHESIS' and 'Authority: None.' Citing a merged synthesis sentence as 'three independent reviews called' is the DR-204 pattern named in the review prompt — a composed statement carried as independent-review standing. The three underlying reviews are not artifacts in this corpus and carry no digests, so the claim is not verifiable from bytes at any grade.
objections.proposedFix: Restate the reason without borrowing reviewer standing, e.g. 'Rejected on D-002's own bytes: the slice's declared state classes exclude durable authoritative commit, so calling it MVP would describe a product the slice cannot be.' That reason is already present in the same bullet and is independently sufficient. If reviewer support is cited at all, cite file 11 as non-binding advice at its digest and reproduce its own support/confidence labels.

objections.claim: The Readiness effect paragraph is true as to set membership but silent about the recalculation constraint step 6 imposes, so a disclosed limitation is incomplete rather than false.
objections.evidence: Draft L241-244: 'Condition 2 is unchanged because D-002's affected-row set is unchanged.' The set membership is indeed unchanged — verified against D-002's condition-2 affected-row set in COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md, which the draft does not alter. But step 6 (L199-201) constrains when that set may be recalculated, which is a change to the condition's operation rather than to its current membership. Under axis 12 a disclosed limitation must be recomputed, and this one under-reports the entry's actual effect.
objections.proposedFix: If C2-D018-02 is repaired by striking 'only', this note falls away. Otherwise extend the Readiness effect paragraph to disclose that step 6 constrains condition-2/4 recalculation.

whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and at end: 920667f9ec1ef5209d5cd0c5779f1f6acd43f28ffee88cfb0b6610354895cd32 both times. The subject did not move during review; the verdict binds these bytes.

Axis 9, citation honesty: all five digests in the draft's measured-inputs table re-measured and CORRECT. File 08 a3e37102991b80502aa1f9fb1affe2011859917b8ce1477a93f494485b9161b7; file 11 ddcd1d3532fd1129c99356c5fd7f1acfab5f2787417392d40b4aa44251fd2cf5; file 07 d3e95060fa81410ae6cd6dc40107d66134fae512db171349dbcba8ea80073a7e; file 10 5378cdbab2d7063fb485bea4b9f7133a92698566e3ec3bdae1e03da415298d18; COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md 3f449778932876ab5039c7f4b35a136a06a67c06b4e2ec00a70e95ae5f3c313f. No wrong digest found. This axis returns clean.

Axis 11, join review: dr105-dr114-join.coherence-independent.json re-measured at 538f368156d22f96bf067dd9faad924610dd78ca16968ad46541efcf14a61344, matching the draft's pin. Read from the verdict bytes and not the draft: $.verdict == 'INCOHERENT' and $.blockers is a 7-element list. The draft's step-3 characterisation is accurate. The verdict's own $.verdictBasis.whatThisVerdictIsNOT records that neither artifact overclaimed, which the draft does not misstate.

Axis 10, DR-008 'integration half': the phrase is genuinely file 08's, not invented by this draft. File 08 line 41, DR-008 status cell: 'PARTIALLY SATISFIED 2026-08-12 — posture half closed, integration half open'. The condition cell also reads 'the EVIDENCE/D9 integration half remains missing'. No new split is created by the draft.

Axis 8, count pins: D-017 Decision 3 pins three members and lists three (arithmetic correct; disjointness contested at C2-D017-02). D-018 Decision 4 pins four rows and lists four — DR-002, DR-004, DR-005, DR-008's integration half. D-018 Decision 6 pins seven steps and lists seven. All three counts are arithmetically correct as stated.

Axis 3, D-002 identity rides: the draft's parenthetical 'four rides on DR-006, one on DR-007' (L162-163) is CORRECT against D-002's Identity-dependencies bytes in COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md — SARIF Run/Finding IDs, cache/regeneration keys, subjectScopeCommitment, and typescriptStdlibMerkleRoot on DR-006; doctor's D9 observation-to-faultCause on DR-007.

Axis 3, DR-130: the draft's claim (L145-147) that 'DR-130 already records that the first slice claims no upgrade continuity' is CORRECT against file 08's DR-130 status cell: 'OPEN — slice 1 claims no upgrade continuity and its deferral disposition is RECORDED HERE (D-010, C-D010)'.

Axis 3, D-002 sets: the draft does not alter D-002's command set, language-role set, platform set, deferral set, or the enumerated condition-2/condition-4 sets. Membership is untouched; the objection at C2-D018-02 is about recalculation rules, not membership, and the objection at C2-D018-03 is about a described product property, not a set.

Axis 4, Route B: the draft does NOT mark any row SATISFIED, does NOT write the dispositions, does NOT waive DR-003 (it expressly requires a scoped threat model at L160-162), and does NOT waive DR-006/DR-007 (it records that both still ride the preview). The closing section reiterates all three non-waivers. The residual defect is the authorization phrasing at C2-D018-04, not a waiver.
Axis 4, docs/v2/implementation/: no sentence in either entry authorizes its creation. The closing section forbids it explicitly and Decision 3 reiterates condition 5.

Axis 2, D-001 five conditions: neither entry quotes them, so the D-001 turn-1 paraphrase-claimed-as-verbatim trap is not sprung. The amendment finding at C2-D018-02 is by operation, not by restatement.

Axis 5: the seven-step sequence at D-018 Decision 6 does not quantify over completion. Step 7 subordinates to file 08 ('Execute the then-current file 08 as the only live plan until D-001's five conditions hold'). It is execution order, not a second readiness list — with the single exception of step 6, raised at C2-D018-02.

Axis 6: no sentence treats file 11 as applying a successor, closing a row, or binding product law. Both entries state the opposite. The residual defect is evidentiary standing at C2-D018-06, not authority.

Axis 12: 'Readiness effect: Zero' for D-017 is TRUE — the entry touches COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md only and moves no file 08 status cell. The closing 'What these two entries do not do' list was recomputed item by item against the draft body and every one of its six clauses holds. D-018's readiness paragraph is incomplete only as noted at C2-D018-07.
Environment stability: all five recorded inputs re-measured at end and unchanged. No finding in this verdict rests on an input that moved after authoring.
whatIDidNotCheck: The other reviewer's verdict file. Not read, per the independence instruction in the review prompt.
Whether the four Route B dispositions, once written, would themselves be lawful or sufficient. They do not exist; this verdict binds only the selection act.

Whether 'architecture preview' is the best available name. Naming is preference-laden and within the coordinator's D-000 authority; my objection C2-D018-03 is to a consequence clause attached to the name, not to the name.

The substance of the DR-105/DR-114 join blockers beyond confirming the verdict string and the blocker count. I read $.verdict and the length of $.blockers, plus $.verdictBasis; I did not adjudicate the seven blockers.

Whether the seven-step sequence is a good execution order. Sequencing is the coordinator's preference-laden call; I checked only whether it is a disguised readiness checklist and whether any step conflicts with adopted bytes.
File 11's own defects. File 11 is not the subject of this review; it is cited only where the draft relies on it.

Any claim about what the three underlying reviewer sessions actually said. Those sessions are not artifacts in this corpus and carry no digests. C2-D018-06 is grounded in file 11's own bytes, not in reviewer recollection.
Whether adopting D-017 without D-018, or D-018 without D-017, creates further inconsistency beyond the coupling noted at C2-D017-04.
